policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere יָּגֶל (short/jussive form) and ketiv יגיל (long imperfect) are spelling variants of the same verb גיל 'rejoice'. ASV 'how greatly shall he rejoice!' renders the verb as a plain future/exclamatory indicative that either form yields; no italicized supply and no textual_variant note is mapped to this unit. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
